document_meta.title: New Jersey 2020 State Forest Action Plan (NJ SFAP)

orientation.summary: The 2020 New Jersey State Forest Action Plan (NJ SFAP) is a state-level forest resource assessment and strategy document produced by the NJDEP Forest Service, fulfilling federal Farm Bill requirements. The document engages extensively with climate change as a central stressor on forest ecosystems, framing it as a 'climate crisis' requiring urgent action. It discusses range shifts explicitly — particularly for tree species, insects (e.g., southern pine beetle northward migration), and Atlantic white-cedar habitat loss to sea-level rise — and incorporates projections from the USDA Climate Change Tree Atlas. The document performs forest inventory analysis using FIA data and references/integrates tool-based results (Tree Atlas, CHANJ connectivity mapping, sea-level rise projections) to inform management decisions, but does not itself run new climate or niche models.

projects: Drexel University studies at Warren Grove Air to Ground Gunnery Range (2011-2013) examined prescribed burning effects on Pine Barren gentian demography, finding positive same-year effects of winter burns on gentian populations, providing evidence that fire management supports climate-adapted rare plant recovery.
